title: RePro: Training Language Models to Faithfully Recycle the Web for Pretraining
claim: Our small rephraser beats much larger prompted baselines on downstream performance while preserving far more source information and contradicting less.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, scatter plus grouped bars with colored delta arrows
description: Two side-by-side plots share one color code for three methods: RePro (4B, dark blue-gray star and bars), ReWire (70B, light blue triangle and bars) and WRAP (7B, green square and bars). Panel (a) is a scatter plot with organic data pool size (72B, 144B, 288B) on the x-axis and DCLM Core Score on the y-axis. Yellow circles mark the organic-only baseline. Each method is labeled with its score, and RePro is highest at 0.299. Panel (b) is a grouped bar chart of the ratio (%) of key points that are supported, omitted or contradicted relative to organic data. Large arrows mark RePro's changes: a green +40% on Support, a red -92% on Omit and a red -18% on Contradict. Captions sit below each panel.
caption: (a) Pretraining performance of 1.4B model and (b) ratio of key points in organic data that are supported / omitted / contradicted in the recycled version across three web recycling methods, computed on 30{,}000 randomly sampled instances. The rephraser size in denoted in parentheses.
abstract: High-quality data is a cornerstone of large language model (LLM) pretraining, yet its growth has not kept pace with the needs of frontier models. In this paper, we introduce RePro, a novel web recycling method that trains a relatively small LM with reinforcement learning to generate effective and faithful rephrasings of pretraining data. Specifically, we design one quality reward and three faithfulness rewards, optimizing the LM rephraser to convert organic data into high-quality rephrasings while maintaining its core semantics and structure. In our experiment, we train a rephraser as small as 1B parameters to recycle 72B tokens sampled from DCLM-RefinedWeb. Pretraining results on 400M, 1.4B, and 2.8B models demonstrate that RePro delivers 3.7%-14.5% relative accuracy gains over organic-only baseline on 22 downstream tasks, doubling the performance gains achieved by the state-of-the-art web recycling method that prompts a 70B rephraser. Experiments with different amounts of recycled data highlight that RePro improves organic data efficiency by 2-3x. Individual and distributional analyses validate that RePro preserves more critical information and faithfully reflects the characteristics of organic data compared to prompting-based methods. Together, these results show that RePro provides an efficient and controllable path to effectively recycle organic data for pretraining. Our code is available at https://github.com/cxcscmu/RePro.
